repo.description: A single file C++ header-only PEG (Parsing Expression Grammars) library

readme.summary: Well-structured documentation with excellent quick start examples and clear PEG syntax reference, though troubleshooting is limited to Linux threading issues.
readme.top_issue: Limited troubleshooting section only covers pthread linking issues for Linux, missing common parsing errors or debugging guidance

injection_risks.description: The code uses system-provided functions like `read_file` and `parser.load_grammar`, but does not directly execute user input as shell commands or SQL queries.
The code uses a PEG grammar to parse the PL/0 language, which may be vulnerable to injection attacks if user input is not properly sanitized.

critical_findings: Potential injection risks due to lack of input validation and sanitization.
Error exposure due to lack of proper error handling mechanisms.
security.summary: The code has some security concerns, including potential injection risks and error exposure, but overall it appears to be well-structured and follows good coding practices.

common_complaints: Parser performance significantly slower than YACC alternatives
Whitespace handling inconsistencies and confusing behavior
Grammar edge cases and nondeterministic parsing failures
